title: Nasdaq-100 annual reconstitution announced after the close — the once-a-year membership list for NDX, effective at the 2027-12-20 open
source: EST: date derived by applying the index owner's own published methodology to the 2027 calendar. The methodology is quoted verbatim from Nasdaq's own index methodology PDF, indexes.nasdaqomx.com/docs/methodology_NDX.pdf, fetched direct 2026-09-08 (HTTP 200, 422,314 bytes, streams inflated and text-extracted in-session): 'Reconstitution Frequency: Annually ... Reconstitution Reference Dates: Last trading day of November ... Reconstitution Announcement Dates: After the close on the sixth trading day prior to the Reconstitution Effective Date ... Reconstitution Effective Dates: At market open on the first trading day following the third Friday in December.' Applied to 2027: the third Friday of December 2027 is 2027-12-17, so the effective date is the next session, MONDAY 2027-12-20; counting back six trading sessions from 2027-12-20 gives 12-17 (1), 12-16 (2), 12-15 (3), 12-14 (4), 12-13 (5) and 12-10 (6), so the announcement lands after the close on FRIDAY 2027-12-10. No US market holiday falls inside that span (Christmas Day 2027-12-25 is a Saturday, observed Friday 2027-12-24, after the whole window), so no session is displaced. Filed estimate on three counts: the date is a forward application of a standing rule rather than a fetched 2027 Nasdaq schedule; the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no member for an index owner's own published methodology (the same gap every S&P DJI and Russell entry on this calendar records); and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. Discovered during the sp-quarterly-rebalance-effective-2027-12-20 initial research, checked 2026-09-08
notes: PROPOSED by the sp-quarterly-rebalance-effective-2027-12-20 initial research (2026-09-08). THIS DISCHARGES A FLAG THE OPEX LANE LEFT OPEN: proposals/opex-2027-12-17.from-consumer-confidence-2027-12-22.json warned that 'December triple witching is the one expiration that also carries annual index reconstitution flow in some index families; this lane did not research that and makes no claim about it.' The family is Nasdaq's, the schedule above is now sourced, and the calendar tracks no Nasdaq-100 reconstitution milestone in any year. THE ANNOUNCEMENT IS PROPOSED AND THE EFFECTIVE DATE IS NOT, and the reason is a measurement. The September 2026 S&P sibling (sp-quarterly-rebalance-effective-2026-09-21) found the ANNOUNCEMENT session, not the effective open, to be where an index-membership change actually reprices — 28 of 32 named companies moved in the direction their index action predicted on the announcement-reaction session, while its own effective open was an index-level null. The proposer then measured the Nasdaq leg directly on 21 December cycles 2005-2026 and found the EFFECTIVE open is a null there too: QQQ's relative volume on that session is the lowest of any bucket measured (0.864x mean / 0.898x median, 6 of 21 above 1.0x), QQQ's third-Friday relative volume shows no December step against its own other quarters (1.264x / 1.233x vs 1.303x / 1.227x, Mann-Whitney p=88.9%), and QQQ's excess return over SPY on the effective open is 7 of 21 negative, sign p=18.9%, MW p=32.6% against every other month. Filing the effective date would put a second measured null on a session this calendar already tracks. WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: any membership names, which will not exist until Nasdaq publishes after the 2027-12-10 close; and any index-level tradeable edge on the announcement itself, which this lane did NOT measure — the S&P sibling's constituent finding is one cycle, one index family, and this house owns no constituent-level instrument to test it with. A taking lane's first job is to check whether the reconstitution announcement moves NDX constituents the way the S&P announcement moved S&P ones, which is the out-of-sample draw that sibling's kill switch asked for. Low impact; proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
